observations: Four photos show large bundles of clothing wrapped in plastic and secured with green straps.
The bundles are tightly packed and appear to contain multiple garments of various colors and patterns.
The plastic wrapping is clear, showing the contents through the mesh of the straps.
No individual garments are visible; only the bundled contents are shown.
The seller's text claims 'UK first-grade clothing' and 'quality, stylish, and affordable'.

claims.evidence: No visible proof of origin or quality standards; the term 'first-grade' is subjective and not verifiable from photos.
Subjective claims; no visual evidence of quality or style beyond appearance in bundles.

risks.risk: Hidden damage or wear on individual garments not visible in bundled photos
risks.proof: Photos of individual garments laid out, showing fabric condition, stains, tears, or tags.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially damaged or worn

risks.risk: Garments are not actually used or are misrepresented as new
risks.proof: Close-up photos of tags, labels, or tags showing condition and care instructions.

risks.risk: Bundles may contain low-quality or counterfeit garments
risks.proof: Photos of tags or labels showing brand, size, and care instructions, or a sample garment with visible brand or tag.

proof_requests: Photos of individual garments laid out, showing fabric condition and any tags or labels.
Close-up photos of tags or labels on the bundles to verify brand, size, and care instructions.

response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
